title: Finishing the width-split round
statement: Let $C$ and $D$ be Boolean Turing machines with positive numbers of work tapes, and choose states $c_e,c_x$ of $C$ and $d_e,d_x$ of $D$. For Boolean words $w,s,u,v$ and a bit $ok$ such that $ok=\mathrm{true}$ implies $|s|\le |w|$, there is a time $t\le 2|u|+2|v|+2|s|+|w|+12$ such that, starting from the configuration in the left-erasure phase with verdict $ok$ and tape words laid out as the candidate $s$ and bank words $u,v$, the controller is not in its anchor state at any time $j<t$. If $ok=\mathrm{true}$, it has halted by time $t$ with output the pair encoding of the prefix of $w$ of length $|s|$ and the remaining suffix; if $ok=\mathrm{false}$, at time $t$ it is in the anchor state with tape words laid out as the candidate obtained by appending one $1$ bit to $s$ when $|s|\le |w|$ (and otherwise leaving $s$ unchanged), and with both banks empty.
hypotheses_covered: $c_e,c_x$ are states of $C$; $d_e,d_x$ are states of $D$
replaced:
Let a verdict bit be given, true only if the candidate's length is at most
$\abs{w}$. Then there is a time
$t \le 2\abs{u} + 2\abs{v} + 2\abs{s} + \abs{w} + 12$ after which the
controller, from the first erasure seam, has erased both installed words
and: on a true verdict, halted with output the pair encoding of the split
of $w$ at position $\abs{s}$; on a false verdict, returned to the canonical
anchored seam carrying one split-search step applied to $s$. No strictly
interior configuration is at the anchor.
